independent_candidates.frame: a sensible person/choice/decision/plan; be sensible; it is sensible to do
independent_candidates.meaning: 分別のある、道理にかなった、現実的な
independent_candidates.rationale: The frame a sensible person/choice/decision/plan; be sensible; it is sensible to do supports the judgment use, where sensible means 分別のある、道理にかなった、現実的な and evaluates a practical choice or action.

semantic_assertions.statement: The adjective evaluates a person, plan, choice, or action as reasonable under real conditions and consequences.
This judgment use must not be generalized to mean high intelligence or guaranteed correctness.

independent_candidates.rationale: The frame sensible shoes/clothes/footwear/coat marks the clothing-and-footwear use, in which sensible means 実用的な、実用本位の and favors function for the situation over fashion alone.

semantic_assertions.statement: With clothing or footwear, sensible describes suitability, durability, comfort-related practicality, or protection for use.
The practical clothing use must not entail that the item is ugly, old-fashioned, or low quality.

independent_candidates.meaning: 感じ取れる、明確に分かる、かなりの
independent_candidates.rationale: The frame a sensible difference/increase/decrease/change identifies the formal perceptibility-and-degree use, where sensible means 感じ取れる、明確に分かる、かなりの rather than reasonable.

semantic_assertions.statement: A difference, increase, decrease, or change described this way must be large or clear enough to be recognized or not ignored.
This formal use must not be read as judging a plan or person to be sensible.

independent_candidates.frame: be sensible to pain/heat/light; sensible to the touch
independent_candidates.meaning: （刺激などを）感じ取れる、知覚できる
independent_candidates.rationale: The frame be sensible to pain/heat/light; sensible to the touch covers the formal or old sensory-capacity use, meaning （刺激などを）感じ取れる、知覚できる for an external stimulus.

semantic_assertions.statement: The to-phrase names an external stimulus that can be received by the senses or body.
This use must not be treated as the ordinary modern equivalent of every meaning of sensitive.

independent_candidates.meaning: ～を意識している、～を深く感じている
independent_candidates.rationale: The frame be sensible of a fact/danger/duty/error/kindness/benefit identifies the formal or literary awareness use, where sensible means ～を意識している、～を深く感じている.

semantic_assertions.statement: The of-phrase names an abstract fact, responsibility, error, danger, kindness, or benefit that is consciously recognized or deeply felt.
The sensible of frame must not be collapsed into sensible to for physical stimulus or into the ordinary judgment adjective.

independent_candidates.frame: sensibly modify a verb, adjective, or whole clause
independent_candidates.meaning: 分別をもって、現実的に、適切に
independent_candidates.rationale: The frame sensibly modify a verb, adjective, or whole clause identifies the adverb sensibly, meaning 分別をもって、現実的に、適切に, rather than another inflected adjective sense.

semantic_assertions.statement: Sensibly functions as an adverb describing a reasonable or practical manner of judging or acting.

independent_candidates.meaning: 分別のあること、現実的であること
independent_candidates.rationale: The frame the sensibleness of a decision/plan identifies the less frequent noun sensibleness, meaning 分別のあること、現実的であること, as a related nominal form.

semantic_assertions.statement: Sensibleness names the quality of being sensible in the judgment or practical sense.

independent_candidates.meaning: 感じない、意識がない、気づかない
independent_candidates.rationale: The frame insensible to pain / insensible identifies a related word meaning 感じない、意識がない、気づかない; it is excluded as a separate headword sense because the article warns that insensible is not a simple opposite across every sensible meaning.

semantic_assertions.statement: Insensible is a separate related adjective and must not be presented as a uniform antonym for every use of sensible.

independent_candidates.frame: sensitive to a stimulus; sensibility as a related noun
independent_candidates.meaning: sensibleと同じ語族に属するが、別の語として覚える関連語
independent_candidates.rationale: The frame sensitive to a stimulus; sensibility as a related noun identifies the neighboring word-family items described by the article as sensibleと同じ語族に属するが、別の語として覚える関連語, not additional forms of the headword.

semantic_assertions.statement: Sensitive and sensibility remain separate lexical items whose meanings cannot be freely substituted for all uses of sensible.

independent_candidates.meaning: 感覚で知覚できるもの（まれな名詞）
independent_candidates.rationale: The frame the sensible (rare noun) represents the rare noun sense 感覚で知覚できるもの（まれな名詞）, which is acknowledged in the usage note but excluded from the main learner-facing adjective senses.

semantic_assertions.statement: The rare noun use must not be allowed to obscure that the main entry is organized around adjective uses.

independent_candidates.rationale: The frame the sensible note (rare music term) represents the rare musical meaning 導音（音楽用語・まれ）, which the article explicitly notes but excludes from the ordinary learner-facing sense list.

semantic_assertions.statement: The rare musical noun or technical use must remain an explicit exclusion rather than being confused with the adjective senses.
